newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech MPs approve border redrawing with Slovakia.
newsitem.headline: Czech MPs approve border redrawing with Slovakia.

text.p: The lower house of the Czech parliament approved on Wednesday a constitutional redrawing of the border with Slovakia set out in a bilateral treaty signed by both governments last year.
The measure, already ratified by Slovakia's parliament, shortens the border by 33 km (21 miles) to 252 km (156 miles), straightening out curves drawn after the split of Czechoslovakia in 1993.
In the most controversial element of the treaty a village in each country will be swapped.
The law was approved on Wednesday by well over the three-fifths majority needed in the Czech lower house, with 141 voting in favour and 37 against.
It is expected to win approval easily in the upper house where the government has a strong majority.

The border change failed in the Czech parliament last April, when only 108 of the house's 200 members voted for the change, as left-wing opposition members and a Moravian national party moved to block the measure.
General elections last June resulted in a consolidation of the house toward the political centre allowing the measure to be resubmitted.
The accord, agreed in January 1996 by both countries' interior ministers, was held up over the sticky issue of swapping the two villages.
The plan calls for the village of U Sabotu to become part of Slovakia and Sidonie to become a Czech community.
The accord would shift a total of 452 hectares (1,117 acres) of land to one or the other side at different spots, allowing the border to follow a more logical line.

A plebiscite in February 1994 asked the residents of the two villages in which country they would want to live. Compensation will be paid to families electing to move elsewhere in order to stay in their original country.
